title: Owners mourn spoiled food after firmware update bricks Samsung smart fridges
gist: A SmartThings firmware update bricked some Samsung Bespoke AI fridges (mostly 2024+ four-door models) in Korea right before the Chuseok holiday, spoiling food and generating hundreds of complaints. Samsung halted the update on September 23 and blamed a testing-process error, while the episode underscores reliability risks of connected appliances.

insights.claim: A firmware update pushed via Samsung's SmartThings platform caused some Samsung Bespoke AI refrigerators, mostly four-door models from 2024 or later, to lose power and stop functioning, showing as offline in the app.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Quality-control failure in Samsung's premium connected-appliance line; potential warranty/repair costs and brand damage.
insights.locator: Affected fridges “suddenly lost power and stopped functioning immediately after”

insights.claim: SBS Korea reported customers filed hundreds of cases over the bricked Samsung fridges, with complaints so far appearing to originate only in Korea.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Scale appears limited and domestic, capping financial impact; Samsung declined to disclose unit counts or countries.
insights.locator: Samsung didn’t respond to Ars’ questions

insights.claim: Samsung stopped issuing the fridge update as of September 23, attributed the failure to an error during the software update testing process, and aimed to fix some units by September 24.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Rapid halt limits spread; watch for compensation announcements.
insights.quote: Yesterday (9/22), an error occurred during the testing process for a Samsung refrigerator software update[.]
insights.locator: Today, a Samsung representative posted a response

insights.claim: The Samsung fridge failures hit just before Korea's food-centric Chuseok holiday, and support agents reportedly said repair technicians might not be available until October.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Poor timing amplified reputational damage in Samsung's home market.
insights.locator: The complaints seem to originate only from Korea

insights.claim: The author argues the obvious way to avoid update-induced failures is to buy appliances that do not receive updates, since a working one- or two-year-old 'dumb' fridge rarely breaks suddenly.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Incidents like this can dent consumer willingness to pay for connected 'AI' appliance premiums.

insights.claim: Abruptly failing connected fridges can cause harms beyond spoiled food, such as ruining medication, illustrating how extraneous technology can spoil a simple product.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Raises potential liability and regulatory scrutiny of over-the-air updates for essential appliances.
insights.quote: extraneous technology can spoil a simple product.
insights.locator: While most of the complaints this week center on rotten food
